# Fertility Tracker

> Live, weekly-refreshed fertility and population data for every country: fertility rate, births, deaths, net migration, immigrant and emigrant stocks, migration corridors, UN projections to 2100 (UN forecast and "if birth rates stay the same"), and a population-decline risk score (0-100) with plain-English reasons. Static JSON/CSV on Vercel: no key, CORS open (Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *).

Sources: World Bank World Development Indicators (latest reported year: fertility 2024, population 2025), UN World Population Prospects 2024 read from the UN's own CSV files with its January 2026 interim update for Togo (estimates 1950-2023, medium-variant and constant-fertility projections 2024-2100; next UN revision 11 July 2027), and UN DESA International Migrant Stock 2024 (via Our World in Data). Every published number is re-checked against these primary sources on each refresh. Codes are ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 (WLD = world, XKX = Kosovo). Numbers are JSON numbers; missing = null. Every record includes iso3, name and region.

## API (base: https://fertility-tracker-live.vercel.app/api/v1/)

- [index.json](https://fertility-tracker-live.vercel.app/api/v1/index.json): manifest with exact source URLs, data vintages, endpoints, known data gaps, generatedAt and contentHash (changes only when numbers change)
- [countries.json](https://fertility-tracker-live.vercel.app/api/v1/countries.json): one summary record per country + WLD: population, tfr, median age, 65+ share, latest births/deaths/net migration (absolute and per 1,000), immigrant/emigrant stock, UN 2050/2100 projection, generation ratio, risk {score, tier, rank, factors}
- [countries/{ISO3}.json](https://fertility-tracker-live.vercel.app/api/v1/countries/KOR.json): everything for one country, including yearly series 1950-2100 (population, births, deaths, naturalChange, netMigration, populationChange, tfr, medianAge, share65), migrant stock history, top 10 origin and destination countries, full risk breakdown, confidence (how sure the numbers are, and what the UN based them on), forecastRange (the UN's 80% and 95% ranges and Zero-migration path, 2024-2100) and crossChecks (newer national figures compared with the UN's)
- [risk.json](https://fertility-tracker-live.vercel.app/api/v1/risk.json): countries ranked by population-decline risk (rank 1 = highest), component points, inputs, factors and the full methodology
- [scenarios.json](https://fertility-tracker-live.vercel.app/api/v1/scenarios.json): population of every country + WLD each year: places[ISO3].estimate (UN estimates 1950-2023, index = year - estimateStartYear), then 2024-2100 under two UN scenarios: places[ISO3].medium ("UN forecast") and places[ISO3].constant ("If birth rates stay the same": fertility held at its 2023 level, mortality and migration as in the forecast); index = year - startYear
- [countries.csv](https://fertility-tracker-live.vercel.app/api/v1/countries.csv): one row per country, nested fields flattened with underscores
- [timeseries.csv](https://fertility-tracker-live.vercel.app/api/v1/timeseries.csv): long format iso3,year,variant,metric,value (variant = estimate | projection), about 11 MB
- [status.json](https://fertility-tracker-live.vercel.app/api/v1/status.json): when the weekly refresh last ran, whether it succeeded, and the deployed commit
- [openapi.json](https://fertility-tracker-live.vercel.app/api/v1/openapi.json): OpenAPI 3.1; JSON Schemas with field descriptions under api/v1/schema/

## Field meanings

- tfr: total fertility rate, births per woman; 2.1 = replacement (each generation the same size)
- population / tfr / share65 / medianAge (and, in country files, birthRate, deathRate, naturalChangeRate, netMigration, populationGrowthPct): {value, year, source}, newest year across sources; source = WB | UN-WPP | UN-DESA
- components: demographic balance for the latest UN estimate year (2023): populationChange = births - deaths + netMigration; perThousand = the same per 1,000 people; migrationOffsetPct = net migration as % of the natural decline (deaths minus births), null when births >= deaths
- migrantStock.immigrants: people living in the country who were born elsewhere (inflow proxy); migrantStock.emigrants: people born there who live abroad (outflow proxy). emigrantsPct = emigrants as % of the current RESIDENT population (UN DESA definition); livingAbroadPct = % of everyone born in the country who lives abroad. Gross annual inflows and outflows are not published globally; use netMigration for the annual flow
- projection: UN WPP medium variant; change2050Pct / change2100Pct are relative to basePopulation in baseYear (latest UN estimate year, 2023), not to the headline population; peakYear; halfPopulationYear; naturalDeclineSince = start of more deaths than births (past or projected)
- share65: % of the population aged 65 or over (100+ included)
- generations.ratio = tfr / 2.1: each ~30-year generation is this fraction of the previous one (100 people -> 100*ratio -> ...)
- risk.score 0-100 = 35 x fertility gap (2.1 -> 0.8) + 15 x natural decline (+5 -> -7 per 1,000) + 10 x aging (65+ share 7 -> 30%, median age 25 -> 50) + 30 x UN-projected decline (2050: 0 -> -25%, weight 1; 2100: 0 -> -60%, weight 2) + 10 x migration not offsetting the decline; each part is a linear ramp clamped to 0..1
- risk.tier: Critical >= 70, High >= 55, Elevated >= 40, Moderate >= 20, Low < 20. risk.rank: 1 = highest risk, null when not ranked (WLD, places under 100,000 people)
- confidence: good | fair | poor, overall (countries.json) and per part (countries/{ISO3}.json: today = last census or register, birthsDeaths = registration complete or estimated, immigration = counted by birth country, citizenship or modelled, forecast = width of the UN's 95% range in 2050). Rules: index.json confidenceRules
- crossChecks[]: {key (today, census, births, deaths, immigrants, net), kind (eurostat, unsd: automatic; researched: hand-checked), figure, unFigure, gapPct = (UN - other) / other x 100, verdict (matches within 2%, un-higher, un-lower, context), links}

## Example calls

- Highest-risk countries: GET api/v1/risk.json -> .ranking[0:10] -> {rank, name, score, tier, factors}
- One country now and in 2050: GET api/v1/countries/JPN.json -> .tfr, .components, .series[] where year == 2050
- A country in 2070 under both scenarios: GET api/v1/scenarios.json -> .places.TWN.medium[2070 - .startYear] and .places.TWN.constant[2070 - .startYear]
- A country in 1990: GET api/v1/scenarios.json -> .places.UKR.estimate[1990 - .estimateStartYear]
- Where a country's emigrants live: GET api/v1/countries/UKR.json -> .migrationCorridors.topDestinations
- How sure a country's numbers are: GET api/v1/countries/NGA.json -> .confidence, .crossChecks; the UN's 95% range in 2050: .confidence.forecast.at[0]
- Spreadsheet: GET api/v1/countries.csv; all years: GET api/v1/timeseries.csv
- Change detection: GET api/v1/index.json -> compare contentHash with your cached copy
